blindSummary: Same-sex conduct is criminalised here — a provision of the 2015 penal code punishes "homosexual conduct" with up to 7 years — and there are no anti-discrimination protections of any kind. This is among the world's most closed states: indefinite national service, mass arbitrary detention, no independent media, no civil society, and no way to document conditions. The country has rejected every SOGI recommendation at every cycle of the UN's periodic human-rights review. Nothing is known about trans people in this country because nothing can be known — the absence of data reflects total informational control.
blindOutOfScope: Documentation absence reflects totalitarian informational control.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): a provision of the 2015 penal code criminalises 'homosexual conduct' with up to 7 years' imprisonment (inherited from the 1957 legal code of the former administering power, with the sentence enhanced after independence). No SOGIESC protections; a foreign government's 2023 human-rights report noted coerced conversion practices undertaken to avoid imprisonment and grossly restricted freedoms; no LGBTIQ organisations; queer people remain closeted for fear of imprisonment and violence.
